issue.title: Use after free in 3.11

labels.name: type-crash
labels.description: A hard crash of the interpreter, possibly with a core dump

issue.body:
When I try to build the current 3.11 0c81909a7a59ea5a6d3af74ac5d2adafe9c8c163 on my 64-bit ArchLinux machine with `clang version 14.0.6` and the following configuration:

```bash
../configure \
    --with-assertions \
    --with-address-sanitizer \
    --with-trace-refs \
    --with-undefined-behavior-sanitizer
```

comments.body: Hmm, this doesn't seem to reproduce all the time..  Might be flaky?

@matthiasgoergens Thanks for the report. Please can you use [git bisect](https://thoughtbot.com/blog/git-bisect) to find when this started in `3.11`? Might be useful to also find when it started and ended in `main` too.

Also ping release manager @pablogsal.

Yes, I'll try bisecting. I'm not sure I have a 100% reliable way to trigger this, so I was suspicious of my previous bisection efforts.

So I'm not even sure, whether it actually went away in main, or whether I just got (un)lucky recently.

See also https://docs.python.org/3.11/whatsnew/changelog.html?highlight=_bootstrap_python#id77 and https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90108 for some info on _bootstrap_python, which was re-introduced in 3.11.

Hmm, whether I can trigger this problem seems to depend on the order in which `make` builds things?

Once I have a binary with the problem, I can trigger it reliably.

But I can't reliably make a binary with the problem.
Preliminarily: it looks like building `--with-pydebug` causes the problem not to show up.  But I'm not sure, because it's flaky for me.

To be honest, I only tested 3.11, because I was trying to do a git bisect to figure out how and when the problem was introduced in main. :)
